answer: A single operator can multiply lookalike keys that all lean the same way and starve honest peers of credit. Bind each new key to a two-stage public trail: first pin a unique work receipt to a timber marker, then after a pause pin a second receipt in a distinct grove, so a burst farm cannot backfill both traces; only then may its text count at the close ledge. The cost is slower first credit for honest thin keys. Verification is the on-chain receipt map plus clustering at close. It fails if a wealthy farm pre-grows clean trails and treats voided receipts as a fee.
